priceSnapshot.note: PROVENANCE FIRST, and the stale-proxy problem is now seven sessions old and it very nearly wrecked this report. The run-proxy fetch of the OKX open-interest endpoint returned 2,117,489,842 USD stamped 2026-09-09T23:03:15Z - 11 hours 27 minutes old - and was DISCARDED. A proxy ticker read taken at 10:30:03 UTC returned 78,205.4, which was fresh AT THAT MOMENT but is now 1,333.0 points above reality. Every number below was re-pulled in-page against okx.com with cache 'no-store' and each payload timestamp checked against wall clock: spot ticker 0.16s, open interest 0.61s, funding 23.3s, the 1H long/short account ratio at the 12:00Z bucket, and the 100 most recent filled BTC-USDT swap liquidations with the newest 6.4 minutes old. This session also ran LATE - 07:54 COT rather than the scheduled 02:00 - so the comparison window against yesterday's endday is 12 hours 15 minutes, not 6. THE ACTUAL STORY: endday's reduce gate fired and then the floor gave way. Against endday's 78,283.0 read, price is 1,410.6 points LOWER, minus 1.80 percent. The path was orderly for ten hours - 78,552.6 high at 04:45 UTC, then a slow bleed through 78,403.5, 78,530.1, 78,423.6, 78,110.8, 78,108.5, 77,998.5 on settled hourly closes - and then it was not. The 10:00 UTC candle closed 77,861.9, the first settled close beneath endday's 77,924.4 reduce level, confirmed by 77,840.0 at 11:00 UTC. Inside the 12:00 UTC hour price fell 1,293.2 points to 76,680.0, and at 12:47:05-12:47:14 UTC - a NINE SECOND window - the OKX tape recorded 100 consecutive sell-side liquidation fills worth 5,771,456 USD with not one buy-side fill among them. changePct is against the rolling 24h open of 79,625.0. Spot has since reclaimed 192.4 points off the low.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below 76,629.9 - the lowest fill price of the 12:47 UTC cascade, 242.5 points under spot and 0.66 hourly ATRs away. This is deliberately placed BENEATH the forced-selling print rather than at it: the cascade already cleared that shelf on the wick, so a wick tag is noise. A settled hourly close underneath it means the market went back for the same level after the levered longs were already gone, which is a different and much worse signal, and it opens the 76,261.0 range floor as the next reference.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE back above 77,051.4, the daily EMA20, which price lost inside the 12:00 UTC hour for the first time since 01 September. 179.0 points above spot. Reclaiming it on a settled close would define the whole move as a wick through a moving average rather than a loss of it, and would be the first evidence that the 5.77 million USD of forced selling was absorbed rather than merely paused.

decisionBox.changed: ADD, and the reason it is ADD rather than REDUCE is the single most important sentence in this report. The lesson log has now blamed the 78,000-79,500 band for SEVEN consecutive losing entries, and every one of those entries was paid for INSIDE that band. Spot is 76,872.4. That is 1,127.6 points BENEATH the bottom of the cursed band, below the entire 1H and 4H EMA stack, and 611.4 points above the 76,261.0 floor that has held this range since 01 September. This is the first time in the series the desk gets to buy outside the zone that has been taking its money. Against that, three things argue for keeping it SMALL and gated, and they are not decorative: the account base got MORE crowded long into the fall, not less, with the 1H long/short ratio running 1.32 at endday to 1.40 now, the highest reading of the week and set while price was making the low; open interest ROSE 83,980,461 USD, plus 4.03 percent, across the same window in which price fell 1.80 percent, which means the notional that left on liquidation was replaced and then some; and funding more than doubled from +0.0000460535 to +0.0001000000, so the remaining longs are paying more to hold a losing position than they were at the top. Macro turned hostile in the same window - Brent is up 4.44 percent to 105.70 on the day, the US 10-year printed 4.904 percent against a 4.84 percent close, and the 09 September ETF row was REVISED from minus 100.7 to MINUS 120.2 million. So: a token spot tranche below the band with a hard 76,261.0 invalidation, and nothing levered.

liquidation.note: 5,504,270 USD of LONG liquidations across 66 sell-side fills - 95.4 percent of every liquidation dollar in the window - inside one 100-point bucket, 172.4 points under spot. These are REALISED fills, executed 12:47:05 to 12:47:14 UTC. The number that matters is not the size but the DURATION: the 100-record feed limit was exhausted by NINE SECONDS of tape, which is the fastest fill rate this dashboard has ever measured and means the true cascade total is larger than 5,771,456 USD - this is a floor, not a total. Carries magnet=true because the bids that absorbed it are gone and have not been replaced; a second visit meets a materially thinner book than the first did.

83,557 USD across 16 sell-side fills, 72.4 points under spot - the upper edge of the same cascade, where it started. Small in dollars and useful only as the marker for where the selling began before it accelerated into 76,700.

180,946 USD across 16 sell-side fills, 272.4 points under spot, and the deepest bucket of the cascade - the lowest individual fill printed 76,629.9. This is the tail of the flush and it is why the reduce gate sits at 76,629.9 rather than at the 76,700 cluster: the market has already proven it can reach here on a wick.

liquidityMagnet.note: The pull is DOWN and the reading is unusually one-sided: of the 100 most recent liquidation fills, ONE HUNDRED were sell-side and ZERO were buy-side, so there is no measured short-liquidation cluster to place above spot and nearestAbove is honestly null rather than guessed. That asymmetry cuts two ways. The bearish reading is that only longs are being carried out and the crowd keeps adding to the losing side - account ratio 1.40, open interest up 4.03 percent, funding doubled positive. The constructive reading is that a 5.77 million USD one-sided cascade compressed into nine seconds is exhaustion behaviour, not distribution, and 15m Wilder RSI at 20.86 is the most oversold intraday reading this dashboard has recorded in this range. Both can be true: the magnet below is real, and the immediate bounce risk for anyone chasing it short is also real.

Open interest is 2,166,776,946.98 USD against endday's 2,082,796,486.28 - UP 83,980,460.70 USD, plus 4.03 percent - while price fell 1.80 percent, so the notional carried out on liquidation was more than replaced. Skew is reported as that 1.40 account ratio because zero buy-side fills makes a dollar-based long/short skew undefined this window. Read together: the leverage got cleaned out at 76,700 and the crowd immediately re-levered long into it, which is exactly the condition that produces a second flush.

calibration.rollingRecord: 10 wins, 8 losses across the last 18 graded sessions. Endday grades a WIN and it is the second in a row, both from the same cause. Since 07 September the chain reads L, L, L, L, W, L, L, W, W. The edge statement written at endday now has one more data point behind it: every win in that chain came from a written level being obeyed on a settled close, and every loss came from a discretionary entry taken inside the 78,000-79,500 band without a level. Two consecutive wins from gates is the first back-to-back the series has produced.
calibration.note: Full accounting of endday's three written levels. THE REDUCE GATE FIRED AND IT WAS RIGHT, BY THE LARGEST MARGIN OF THE SERIES. It required a settled 1H close below 77,924.4. The 10:00 UTC candle closed 77,861.9, clearing the trigger by 62.5 points, and 11:00 UTC confirmed at 77,840.0, 84.4 points through. Price then fell to 76,680.0 inside the next hour, so obeying the first settled close avoided 1,181.9 points of further drawdown from the trigger and 1,603.0 points from endday's 78,283.0 report price. Spot marks 76,872.4, which is 1,052.0 points BELOW the gate - unlike midday's reduce, this one has NOT handed the re-entry back, and a trader who obeyed it is still ahead and still in cash. THE ADD GATE REFUSED, AND IT WAS CLOSE. It required a settled 1H close above 78,611.2. The session high was 78,552.6 - short by 58.6 points - and the best settled hourly close was 78,530.1 at 05:00 UTC, short by 81.1 points. That is the narrowest refusal the series has recorded and it was worth 1,872.6 points to the eventual low. A 58.6-point miss saved 2.4 percent, which is the whole argument for demanding settled closes instead of touches. THE INVALIDATION AT 76,261.0 was not tested; the low was 76,680.0, 419.0 points above it. THE RECOMMENDED RESTING STOP AT 77,924.4 WOULD HAVE BEEN FILLED and it would have been RIGHT by 1,052.0 points against current spot - the FIRST session in five in which recommending the stop was the correct call rather than declining it, which is exactly what should happen when the gap actually contains the event. Net: the gate fired and won large, the add gate refused by a hair and won large, the invalidation was never reached, and the stop recommendation finally paid. Four for four on written levels.
